transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-18
Time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 58 min
Attendees: Maya Singh (Redwood AE), Jon Park (Redwood SE), Lina Morales (Product), Dr. Elena Ruiz (CTO - OrchidBio), Samir Patel (SRE), Tessa Huang (Lead Data Engineer), Alex Gomez (Security)

Auto-summary (brief):
Purpose: live walkthrough of Redwood Console request traces, KV cache behavior, error triage workflow, and private deployment telemetry options. Customer asked about PHI handling, replay/privacy modes, retention and runbook integrations. Agreed actions: KV-cache stress test, send security packet and installer docs, pilot kickoff planning.

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Maya: Thanks all for joining, quick intros then Jon will take the console and Lina will chime on product & retention.
[00:00:12] Dr. Elena: Hi, thanks. Our ask is pragmatic: in a recent incident we spent hours chasing whether the issue was model, runtime or our input normalization. Can your trace tooling narrow that down faster?
[00:00:25] Jon: Absolutely. We'll pull up the request explorer, show trace timelines, and then a failing request example that ties into GPU/memory metrics and KV-cache events. Note: demo env has scrubbed names, sometimes the auto-transcript mangles component names.
[00:00:40] Samir: Quick constraints: PHI must remain in our VPC for prod, audit retention 24 months, SSO via SAML, and SRE on-call only paged for payment or consent routes. p50/p95/p99 latency targets are 150/700/1000ms.
[00:00:58] Lina: Got it - SAML and RBAC supported, retention configurable, private install option for control plane inside your VPC.
[00:01:10] Tessa: When you show KV-cache hits, is that per-session prefix cache or global? We need TTL tunability and key visibility.
[00:01:20] Jon: We expose both prefix-level caching in the runtime and request-level KV entries. TTLs and sampling are configurable and you can inspect key age and entropy on the trace timeline.
[00:01:32] Alex: Security question - do you persist raw prompts in hosted mode? How is encryption handled?
[00:01:40] Maya: Encrypt in transit and at rest. You can enable redaction at ingestion so prompts are masked or dropped before storage. For private installs you control KMS.
[00:01:52] Jon: I'm sharing screen now, opening Console -> Projects -> Orchid-sim. Request explorer visible.
[00:02:05] [screen share noises]
[00:02:15] Jon: Here's a request flagged as error: error tag shows 'kv-cache-fallback' and p99 spike. Clicking into trace reveals frames: ingress -> parse -> route -> runtime -> model -> postprocess. Each frame has start/end timestamps and attached logs.
[00:02:33] Dr. Elena: kv-cache-fallback - does that mean cache entry corrupted or TTL expired?
[00:02:40] Jon: Could be both. Our event stores a reason code: miss/invalid-hash/serialization-error. In hosted mode some identifiers are pseudonymized; in private you get full keys if you opt in.
[00:02:55] Samir: Can we alert on fallback rate? We need to correlate fallback rate with p99 spikes.
[00:03:02] Lina: Yes, alerting UI lets you select metrics like fallback_rate + p99 latency and scope by route. Composite alerts supported.
[00:03:12] [00:03:20] Jon: Expanding the timeline, you can see a kernel selection note - the runtime used a quantized kernel and also logged a small numeric-delta metric. If the delta threshold is exceeded, Optimize will flag it as 'numeric drift'.
[00:03:35] Dr. Elena: Could numeric drift cause subtle QA regressions?
[00:03:40] Jon: In edge cases yes. We surface token-level diffs in the trace and can link to your golden sets in Optimize.
[00:03:50] Tessa: For private installs, does the console ship metrics to Redwood or stay local? We want aggregated telemetry for support but not raw prompts.
[00:03:58] Lina: You can host observability locally. There's an opt-in anonymous metrics pipe for product support that sends aggregated counters only; raw traces stay in your network unless you opt-in.
[00:04:10] [00:04:20] Jon: Back to the failing trace - notice at 00:00:14 the runtime recorded a memory pressure event coincident with fallback. We also capture node_id and kernel_version for each frame.
[00:04:32] Samir: How long are traces retained by default? Audit needs 24 months.
[00:04:38] Lina: Hosted defaults 90 days; enterprise retention add-ons extend that. Private installs, retention is customer-controlled.
[00:04:48] Alex: For PHI we need redaction and field-level masking, meaning operators cannot see original prompt. Support access must be gated.
[00:04:56] Maya: We support regex and ML-based ingestion redaction hooks and strict access controls; we'll include the access matrix in the packet.
[00:05:06] Jon: Now demonstrating replay - we can replay a sanitized request against a pinned model in an isolated sandbox. If you prefer prompts never stored, we store a hashed envelope and replay uses customer-supplied prompt artifacts.
[00:05:22] Tessa: How do replays handle webhooks or external tool calls?
[00:05:26] Lina: Replays can be configured to call your mock endpoints or be run against a defined mock framework. We capture tool-call metadata so replay can simulate tool interactions.
[00:05:36] [00:05:45] Jon: On sampling overhead - tracing is async and adds microseconds. Heavy captures are sampled or conditional on errors. You can set sampling policy per environment to keep p99 overhead minimal.
[00:05:58] Samir: We need overhead to be <10ms p99.
[00:06:02] Jon: That's achievable with conservative sampling and async buffers; we'll include recommended configs.
[00:06:12] [00:06:20] Jon: Showing the KV-cache analytics - dashboard shows hit/miss rates, key entropy, and fallback reasons over time. For this failing window you can see a cluster of fallbacks after a kernel JIT event.
[00:06:35] Dr. Elena: Kernel JIT? That triggered the spike?
[00:06:38] Jon: The trace shows a compile step took ~250ms on first request; later requests used cached kernels. You can pre-warm kernels at deploy or via warm-up API to avoid first-hit penalty.
[00:06:50] Tessa: Can we run a stress test to exercise bursts and fallback behavior? Output format should be timeseries and CSV for integration with our tools.
[00:06:58] Jon: We'll run a KV-cache stress plan (replay 50k requests with varied key distributions) and output dashboards + CSVs with per-request fallback reasons and latency deltas.
[00:07:10] Samir: We'll need to simulate GPU saturation and also test model fallback to smaller variants.
[00:07:15] Maya: We'll include burst simulations in the test plan.
[00:07:22] [00:07:30] Jon: Incident/runbook features - alerts can include runbook links and the console can pre-fill a postmortem template with trace id, node ids, model version, and suggested mitigations (pin kernel, increase memory). You can export to Jira or your ticketing system.
[00:07:45] Dr. Elena: Good, we want auto-populated runbooks. Also can you diff two traces token-by-token?
[00:07:52] Jon: Yes, trace diff shows token-level logits and highlights divergence. Exportable as JSON or side-by-side HTML.
[00:08:05] Alex: For hosted mode who has access to traces? We need roles and human access justification.
[00:08:12] Maya: We'll include internal access policy in the security packet; typically support access is audited and gated, elevated access is rare and incident-scoped.
[00:08:20] Samir: SIEM integration - can traces stream to our Splunk? Field mappings?
[00:08:26] Lina: You can stream JSON traces to S3 or syslog; we provide a mapping template for Splunk ingestion to align with your fields. Sampling recommended to control volume.
[00:08:40] [00:08:50] Jon: Demo of a quality regression alert: Optimize compared outputs to a golden set and flagged an output drift. From the alert you can jump to traces and see model/kernel differences.
[00:09:02] Tessa: If a regression triggers in canary, can deployment automatically rollback?
[00:09:06] Jon: Yes, there are automatic abort/fallback policies you can configure for canaries.
[00:09:14] Dr. Elena: Installer questions - does private installer include the console UI? We want the UI inside our network.
[00:09:20] Lina: Yes, the private package includes control plane components, Console UI, and observability services to run inside your VPC. Helm charts and an airgap tarball available.
[00:09:32] Alex: We'll need the list of required ports and architecture diagram.
[00:09:36] Maya: We'll attach network diagram and endpoint list in follow-up.
[00:09:44] [00:09:55] Jon: A quick note on identifiers - use trace id & node id as canonical keys because short service names in transcripts can be ambiguous.
[00:10:02] Samir: About cost visibility - can we see per-request cost, token breakdown, and cost by model variant?
[00:10:08] Lina: Yes, Console provides token-level cost breakdowns and per-route cost dashboards, plus budget/quotas by environment.
[00:10:18] Tessa: Dev noise inflates cost - we need per-environment budgets and alerts.
[00:10:22] Maya: Supported - we'll show billing UI in follow-up.
[00:10:30] [00:10:40] Jon: Running through the planned KV-cache stress steps: pre-warm vs no pre-warm, 50k replay with varied key entropy, collect fallback reasons, p50/p95/p99 latency deltas, memory pressure; deliver CSV + dashboard.
[00:10:58] Dr. Elena: For replays, we must ensure prompts flagged as PHI are never persisted; how is that enforced?
[00:11:04] Jon: Ingestion hooks can mask or drop prompt text. Replay can accept customer-supplied sanitized artifact instead of a stored prompt. We'll document privacy mode.
[00:11:16] Alex: HSM/KMS support for on-prem keys?
[00:11:20] Maya: Yes, HSM-backed KMS supported in private deployments.
[00:11:26] Samir: Do you provide a list of subprocessors for procurement?
[00:11:30] Maya: Yes, that will be in the security packet.
[00:11:36] [00:11:45] Jon: About sampling: heavy traces are conditional, stack dumps are error-only unless you enable high-fidelity sampling. That keeps tracing overhead low.
[00:11:56] Tessa: We want sampling guidance tuned for our p99 constraint.
[00:12:00] Jon: We'll include recommended sampling configs in the KV test deliverable.
[00:12:08] [00:12:20] Jon: Wrapping: shown request explorer, trace timeline, KV cache events, kernel/jit notes, replay, diffing, alerts, runbook exports, and private install options.
[00:12:35] Dr. Elena: Next steps?
[00:12:38] Maya: Redwood: send SOC2 and network diagram, share Helm charts and installer docs, run KV-cache stress tests and send results, propose pilot kickoff Jan 25. Orchid: share sample traces and confirm runbook owners.
[00:12:52] Samir: We'll aim to send traces by 2027-01-21 and confirm pilot scope by 2027-01-20.
[00:12:58] Alex: Security will run checklist and revert.
[00:13:05] Maya: I'll follow up with email and attachments.
[00:13:10] Jon: Any final questions?
[00:13:14] Tessa: One small item - when exporting for Splunk can you provide a mapping template?
[00:13:19] Jon: Yes, we'll provide mapping templates.
[00:13:24] Maya: Thank you all, we'll send the packet and the test plan.
[00:13:30] Dr. Elena: Thanks everyone, helpful session.
[00:13:35] [end of recording - brief chatter]
